text:
noah: Hey finance — hotel charged a $30 'late checkout' fee to the Redwood corpcard in NYC. I checked out late bc of a client call. Hotel won't email a folio, front desk says it's on the folio at checkout but I didn't get a copy. Can I still expense? cc @tasha
tasha: Did front desk provide any on-screen confirmation or a folio number? If corpcard was used we need either folio or a manager sign-off. Do you have the AMEX transaction screenshot?
noah: I have the AMEX transaction and a photo of the final bill screen (it shows the fee line but no folio number). I also have the client meeting invite that overlaps checkout window.
sam: Policy: hotel incidental fees on corpcard need folio or manager approval if no folio available. Since it's business-related and under $50 we can accept manager approval + backup docs. @noah please upload to Expensify and tag me in notes.
noah: Uploaded: https://expensify.com/report/late-checkout-nyc (attached). Notes: "client call ran late, manager tasha approved". AMEX screenshot and bill-photo attached.
expensify-bot: Expense received: Report late-checkout-nyc, total $30.00, status 'Submitted'  awaiting finance review.
tasha: I approve this one-off. Confirming business necessity: client call ran until 11:30am, checkout at 1pm. Approved.
sam: Approved by manager + finance. We'll reimburse $30 and note missing folio. One bookkeeping note: include corpcard last4 (e.g., `XXXX-4321`) in the expense so payments ops can reconcile.
noah: Added last4 and updated notes. One more Q: teammate Jen was on the same trip and paid parking on her personal card — should she submit separate or can we group?
tasha: Separate reports is fine. Noah, finance will process your $30. Jen should submit her parking with receipts and indicate it's personal card expense.
payments-bot: Case logged: VM-2034 reconciliation note added for missing folio; flag cleared with manager approval. Expected reimbursement in next payroll (~10 business days).
noah: Thanks all :pray:
